overrides.reason: ZGEEV hands its LWORK to ZGEHRD, ZUNGHR, ZHSEQR and ZTREVC3, which pick their block size, AED window or back-transformation from LWORK. The blocked and unblocked Hessenberg reductions round differently, and the QR iteration that follows can then deflate the eigenvalues in another order, so W, the Schur form T in A (also unique only up to unit phases), and the eigenvector columns that follow W's order all change. The reference does this as well: compiled LAPACK 3.12.0 ZGEEV (random matrix, JOBVR = 'V') returns a different A and a different order of W at LWORK = 2N than at its optimum for N = 150, 200 and 300. The JS zgehrd crosses over at NX = 32 where ILAENV(3) gives 128, so the JS path changes from N > 33 (the reference's from N > 128): at N = 80 and 120 the JS result at WORK = 2N is bit-identical to the one with only zgehrd held unblocked, and matches the optimum's spectrum to 5e-14 with 4 and 18 eigenvalues reordered and the matched eigenvectors equal to 2e-14. The module's tests check the spectrum and the eigenvector residuals at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (ticket 0100).

set.params.A.workDependent: the Schur form T follows the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change, and is unique only up to unit phases
set.params.w.workDependent: the order in which the eigenvalues deflate depends on the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking
set.params.VL.workDependent: the eigenvector columns follow the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
set.params.VR.workDependent: the eigenvector columns follow the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
